answer: Unique-seed divergence check. Each identity is assigned a random seed; its first action derives a response from that seed and a shared ocean of public inputs, and the output is logged. Enforcement rule: no two identities may return byte-identical derivations, since true independent agents diverge under the same inputs while clones collide. An attacker cloning one agent to a summit of N copies must run N distinct seed executions, paying N times the compute and storage to keep every thread unique.
